g_policy.reason: The user taps to play, so it is opt-in. The offer copy states the reward (3 Advanced reasoning mode answers today), 'Not now' leaves home unchanged, and the ad-fail path hides the card or shows a retry.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 3 Advanced reasoning mode answers until midnight, which cannot be withdrawn, transferred or exchanged.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is the first app open after 3 or more days without a session by a non-subscriber, which is an app event and needs no chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: It adds a sample and removes or caps nothing free; the proposal says 'removes nothing free: yes'. Advanced reasoning mode is a paywall feature (l02), not a free one.

g_brand_safety.reason: The card sits under the header on s01 Chats home, which is rated safe. It is app chrome on a non-chat screen and not inside any conversation.

c1_revealed_value.reason: The app charges for the resource, since 'Advanced reasoning mode' (s02.e03, l02) is a bullet on the Luzia+ paywall behind Weekly, Monthly and Annual plans.

c2_evidence.reason: The paywall feature (s02.e03), the home upsell badge (s01.e02), the trial button (s02.e19) and the 'How can I help you today?' prompt (s01.e08) are all observed. The reward is honestly labelled as inference.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward is limited to 3 answers and expires at midnight, with a 1-per-day cap and a 3+ day gap. That is a time- and quantity-limited sample.

c5_moment.reason: The card appears on the home screen at app open, before any task has started. It is dismissible and does not interrupt anything.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn sponsored game, and the card only changes to 'answers ready' after the play is confirmed. The trigger is a detectable session-gap event.

c7_specific.reason: It names Luzia's Advanced reasoning mode, the Luzia+ paywall and badge, the Chats home prompt card and the 3-day trial, so it would not read the same in another app.

other_concern: How Advanced reasoning mode is selected or used in chat was not observed, and neither was a free-tier limit on it. The cost-recovery rationale is speculative, and the 1-answer fallback for lower-earning markets is not part of the offer itself.
